analysis.title: Up and Adam, daily market note for Thursday, November 19, 2026
key_insights: For the first time since April 7, the S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq Composite and Russell 2000 are all trading below their 200-day moving averages. 49% of S&P 500 stocks are below their own 200-day average, versus a five-year average of 43%.

The report argues the technical break is not necessarily bearish. Over the past 20 years, when the S&P 500 traded below its 200-day average, the median 12-month return was 10.9%, with gains 78% of the time.

Pending home sales fell 4.7% month over month in October, more than expected, and the 16.7% year-over-year decline was the steepest since 2023. The level is the lowest since the National Association of Realtors began tracking in 2001, with every region down on the month and the year.
The report cites median home prices of $416k near record highs and mortgage rates at 7.35%. It expects sluggish housing activity to drag on economic growth going into 2027.

Gamers spent an estimated $1.65 billion preordering Grand Theft Auto VI ahead of its release, per Sensor Tower. Target, Home Depot, Lowe's and TJX also reported upbeat earnings this week, which the report reads as resilient consumer spending despite inflationary pressure.
Consumer Discretionary leads all sectors month to date at +4.9%, against -3.4% for the S&P 500. The report reaffirms its overweight to the sector.

The US Dollar Index is at its highest level since March 2025 and has risen another 0.9% since last week. Gold and silver are at 14-month lows, and zinc, copper and cobalt are at 4-, 7- and 14-month lows.
Falling metal prices hurt Materials miners. The report says lower input costs could lift margins for manufacturers in Consumer Discretionary and Industrials.
Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth. The report uses it to argue for staying invested, noting the S&P 500 has risen more than 7,400% since September 1977.

sector_views.rationale: Sector leads month to date at +4.9% versus -3.4% for the S&P 500, and upbeat Target, Home Depot, Lowe's and TJX earnings point to resilient spending. Lower metal input costs could also help margins.
Lower commodity input costs could boost margins for manufacturers. The report states no formal stance.
Falling metal prices are unwelcome for miners. The report states no formal stance.

earnings_insights: Target, Home Depot, Lowe's and TJX each reported upbeat earnings this week (reported). The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Housing contract activity is at its lowest since NAR tracking began in 2001, reinforcing the report's view of a housing drag on growth into 2027.
Steepest annual decline since 2023, with every region posting monthly and annual declines.
Together with median home prices of $416k near record highs, affordability keeps housing activity weak.
Consensus expects a lower reading than the prior release. Scheduled for 8:30am ET on 11/19.

risk_factors: Broad technical weakness, with all four major US equity benchmarks below their 200-day averages.
Housing affordability: record-high median prices and 7.35% mortgage rates are a drag on growth into 2027.
A stronger US dollar is pressuring metal prices, which hurts miners in the Materials sector.
Inflationary pressure continues alongside resilient consumer spending.
